name: NVIDIA cuda-samples matrixMul
listed_description: Official CUDA sample implementing tiled shared-memory matrix multiplication; the book says its own optimized kernel follows the same approach.
reason: No number in the repo and no claim that matrixMul beats any baseline. The sample README (cpp/0_Introduction/matrixMul, opened) says the kernel is 'written for clarity of exposition ... not with the goal of providing the most performant generic kernel', the top-level README says the samples 'are not intended for performance benchmarking', and matrixMul.cu (opened) only prints 'Performance= ... GFlop/s' at run time, with no stored result, no naive-kernel variant and no cuBLAS call (cuBLAS is in the separate matrixMulCUBLAS sample). The only comparison found is a 2013 personal-blog post seen only as a search snippet (page blocked, EGRESS_BLOCKED): matrixMul about 127 GFlop/s versus matrixMulCUBLAS about 452 GFlop/s on a GTX 560, i.e. the sample is slower than cuBLAS, so it is no win and unverified. BSD-3-Clause style licence header (Copyright 2022 NVIDIA), 9.7k stars, last commit 2026-09-09.
